branches.title: Why does each match keep only the smaller value?
branches.source:
Got it, I'll remember your bracket codename, AMBER-HERON-42, for the rest of our conversation.

The eight numbers start as leaves and are paired off, and each pair's smaller value "wins" and advances to the next round. The four winners are paired again, then the two survivors face off, so after three rounds (7 comparisons total) one value reaches the root. That champion at the root is the minimum, because it never lost a comparison to any other number.

branches.source: Because we're hunting for the minimum, the larger value in any match has just been beaten by something smaller, so it can't possibly be the minimum and is safely discarded. Keeping only the smaller value means each winner is the minimum of everything below it, so the value that reaches the root is the minimum of all eight numbers.
